subject.title: Feature: post-process NO_REPLY to suppress partial leaks

question: Should OpenClaw broaden `NO_REPLY` suppression for mixed trailing or own-line payloads, and where is the boundary between silent-intent internal text and legitimate substantive replies that append or mention the token?
rationale: Current main intentionally preserves some mixed trailing-token replies, while the issue asks for broader suppression to prevent internal text leaks; that is a shared message-delivery and security contract choice rather than a mechanical cleanup close.

options.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
options.body: Define a shared classifier that suppresses internal or silent-intent mixed payloads, preserves legitimate substantive replies, and is reused by every delivery path.

options.title: Use blanket trailing or own-line suppression
options.body: Suppress any reply ending with a trailing or own-line `NO_REPLY` token, accepting that some currently visible substantive replies may be dropped.

options.title: Keep the narrow current policy
options.body: Document that only token-only, punctuation-only, and reasoning-prefixed silent payloads are suppressed, then retarget broad suppression requests.

recommendation.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
recommendation.body: Define a shared classifier that suppresses internal or silent-intent mixed payloads, preserves legitimate substantive replies, and is reused by every delivery path.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans shared reply delivery and security/product policy, and steipete is the clearest routing candidate from the central behavior's commit history.
